notes: The `לוֹ` of 'she shall be his wife' is read under rule 40: the preposition is unrepresented and the suffix takes 'his'. Rule 49's closing paragraph would instead fuse a belonging `לְ` written as an English genitive into the following word's unit. The rule 40 reading is preferable here because 'his' is exactly the pronoun a bare suffix would produce, so no separate English answers to the preposition — unlike `לַיהוָה` → 'is Jehovah's', where the genitive marker carries the relation. Worth recording as the live alternative.
The italic 'shekels' supplies a measure noun the Hebrew never writes and is added under rule 33, while the 'of' stands before the written kesef and belongs to it.
The supplied 'them' after 'give' answers to no object morpheme and is added under rule 44.
